cards.placement: During the narrator's L003, synced to the moment the narrator says "Tara". Simple caption over its own separate, unlocated landscape (a forest reaching a cliff edge; shotlist.json P-10). One name per landscape: no other named place or sea in the same view. No map, no borders, no arrows.
cards.screenplay_says: PICTURE: A broad series of landscapes: a coastal settlement, open sea, a forest reaching a cliff, distant fortified walls. Use dissolves rather than a fake precise map. If place names appear, show them as simple captions over unlocated sea or land, without implying boundaries: TARA; CITADEL SEA; SCRAPPER; PROXY SEA; VERDOR.
cards.note: Proposed production choice: the captions follow the narrator's order in L003 (Tara, Scrapper, Verdor, Citadel Sea, Proxy Sea), each appearing as its name is spoken. The screenplay's own caption list is in a different order (TARA; CITADEL SEA; SCRAPPER; PROXY SEA; VERDOR). The captions are optional and can be dropped.

cards.placement: Harbor intercut in Scene 2C: either a restrained identification card or lettering on the ship's hull, only if it can be read clearly.
cards.screenplay_says: PICTURE: Brief harbor intercut. The messenger runs down weathered steps, reaches a waiting crew, and delivers the order without repeating the whole scene. Show the Santa Maria's name on a restrained identification card or its hull only if the production design supports legible lettering. This is the story's vessel, not an excuse to import historical Earth figures.
cards.note: The story's own vessel, not a reference to historical Earth figures. It does not need to be shown at all.

cards.placement: Opening of Scene 3A, over the festival already in motion at human height.
cards.note: Not marked optional. The final period in the screenplay is punctuation, not part of the caption. Cling is a kingdom within Scrapper.

cards.placement: Scene 3B, on the controlled close shot introducing her face on Starlight. Never label her Alexandria.
cards.screenplay_says: PICTURE: Cut high above the village to Queen Fall riding Starlight. Introduce her face in a controlled close shot, then re-establish her smallness against her dragon. Do not label her Alexandria. A brief non-spoken identification in the production notes is enough; an on-screen name is optional.
cards.note: The screenplay says a production-note identification is enough and an on-screen name is optional. Exact wording is not fixed; 'QUEEN FALL' is the plainest form.
